1	Heavy machines are frequently installed above the surface that carries them. A rooftop unit may have to stand clear of a membrane, a shop machine may have to stand clear of a wash-down floor, and equipment carried on a vehicle bed may have to stand clear of the bed itself. When the required standoff height is not known until the machine is in place, or when the height has to change later, a fixed pedestal or a stack of shims is inconvenient, because setting or resetting the height means lifting the machine off the support again.
2	
3	A height-adjustable platform avoids that lifting, but it introduces three problems that a design must solve together before such a platform can carry a heavy machine dependably.
4	
5	The first problem is parallelism. If each corner of a deck is adjusted through its own screw, jack, or shim stack, the corners are adjusted one after another. The deck twists and cocks in its guides while the adjustment is in progress, the guided members bind against their guides, and the finished height at one corner differs from the finished height at another, so that the machine is left out of level and the guides are left preloaded.
6	
7	The second problem is load holding. A drive train that both moves the deck and holds it is a single load path. Its gearing, its fasteners, and its input coupling all have to carry the standing weight of the machine for as long as the machine is installed, and any wear, backlash, or maintenance operation on that drive train is a wear, backlash, or maintenance operation on the only thing supporting the load.
8	
9	The third problem is the state of the locks. Where a platform is held by separate mechanical locks, those locks must be released to adjust the height and must be returned afterwards. Two failure modes follow. A lock that is only partly released is dragged across the toothed member it engages while the platform is being adjusted, which damages the tooth flanks it will later have to sit on, and a lock that is never returned leaves the platform standing on its drive train while looking, from the outside, exactly like a platform that is locked. Where several locks are pulled by one linkage through separate flexible connections, ordinary differences in connection length make the partly released condition the normal condition rather than the exception, because the shortest connection lifts its lock first and the longest connection may not lift its lock at all.
10	
11	There remains a need for a reusable height-adjustable equipment platform that changes the height of every guided post of a deck by the same distance from a single input, that holds the resulting height through load locks that are independent of the drive train, that releases every one of those load locks together despite differences in the lengths of the flexible connections that pull them, and that shows the operator, before the platform is loaded, that every load lock has in fact returned.
12

3	Overall arrangement
4	
5	Referring to FIG. 1, a reusable height-adjustable equipment platform comprises a base frame 10 that rests on a support surface 64 and an equipment deck 12 that is carried above the base frame 10 and remains parallel to the base frame 10 at every height. The support surface 64 may be a roof, a floor, a vehicle bed, or any other surface able to carry the platform and the machine mounted on it. The base frame 10 is a rectangular frame. The equipment deck 12 receives the machine it supports, for example through mounting holes, rails, or clamps at the upper face of the equipment deck 12, and the machine remains on the equipment deck 12 while the height of the equipment deck 12 is changed.
6	
7	The base frame 10 carries four upright guide towers 14, one near each corner of the base frame 10. The equipment deck 12 carries four corner posts 16, one depending from each corner of the equipment deck 12. Each corner post 16 slides vertically in a respective one of the guide towers 14, so that the four guide towers 14 together restrain the equipment deck 12 against horizontal displacement and against tilting, and leave it free to move vertically. Each guide tower 14 is a hollow upright member whose interior corresponds to the cross section of the corner post 16 that slides in it, and bearing surfaces at the upper and lower ends of the interior of the guide tower 14 take the horizontal reactions produced by an off-centre machine on the equipment deck 12.
8	
9	Each corner post 16 carries a rack 18 extending along the corner post 16 in the direction of travel. In the illustrated embodiment the rack 18 lies along an inward-facing side of the corner post 16, that is, the side of the corner post 16 that faces the interior of the base frame 10. Placing the rack 18 on the inward-facing side keeps the toothed face of the rack 18 and the members that engage it inside the footprint of the platform, where they are shielded from weather and from impact, and lets an operator reach the drive members of all four guide towers 14 from within the base frame 10.
10	
11	A pinion 20 is mounted in each guide tower 14 and meshes with the rack 18 of the corner post 16 that slides in that guide tower 14, so that rotation of the pinion 20 raises or lowers that corner post 16 and the corner of the equipment deck 12 attached to it. Each pinion 20 is journalled in the guide tower 14 so that the mesh with the rack 18 is maintained over the whole travel of the corner post 16.
12	
13	A removable cover 60 closes the base frame 10 over the drive members and the release members described below. Removing the removable cover 60 gives access to the worm drive, the sprockets, the synchronizing chain, the locking pawls, the release cables, and the cable adjusters for inspection, lubrication, and adjustment without removing the equipment deck 12 and without taking the machine off the equipment deck 12.
14	
15	A release handle 52 projects from the base frame 10 where an operator standing beside the platform can reach it, and a hand crank 36 is inserted into the base frame 10 at the same side to drive the platform. The release handle 52 and the hand crank 36 are the only two members the operator handles, and the sequence in which they may be handled is enforced mechanically, as described below.
16	
17	Synchronized drive
18	
19	A front transverse shaft 22, a rear transverse shaft 24, and a worm input shaft 32 are journalled in the base frame 10, within the space that the removable cover 60 closes.
20	
21	Referring to FIG. 2, the two pinions 20 at the front of the platform are fixed to the front transverse shaft 22 and the two pinions 20 at the rear of the platform are fixed to the rear transverse shaft 24. Each of the front transverse shaft 22 and the rear transverse shaft 24 extends from one side of the platform to the other, so that the two pinions 20 fixed to it necessarily rotate through the same angle.
22	
23	A front sprocket 26 is fixed to the front transverse shaft 22, a rear sprocket 28 is fixed to the rear transverse shaft 24, and one endless synchronizing chain 30 runs over the front sprocket 26 and the rear sprocket 28. The front sprocket 26, the rear sprocket 28, and the endless synchronizing chain 30 together form a synchronizing transmission that couples all four pinions 20 for rotation together. Because all four pinions 20 rotate together and all four racks 18 have the same pitch, every corner post 16 travels by the same distance for a given input rotation, the equipment deck 12 rises and falls parallel to the base frame 10, and the corner posts 16 do not cock in the guide towers 14. The equipment deck 12 is therefore not racked in the guide towers 14 at any point during a height change, rather than being brought back to parallel after a sequence of separate corner adjustments.
24	
25	The worm input shaft 32 carries a worm that drives a worm wheel 34 fixed to the front transverse shaft 22. Rotation of the worm input shaft 32 therefore rotates the front transverse shaft 22, and through the endless synchronizing chain 30 the rear transverse shaft 24, and through the four pinions 20 the four corner posts 16. The worm input shaft 32 and the worm wheel 34 form a rotary input to the synchronizing transmission. The mesh between the worm of the worm input shaft 32 and the worm wheel 34 is a high-reduction mesh that resists back-driving of the synchronizing transmission by the weight on the equipment deck 12, so that the equipment deck 12 does not run down when the input torque is removed and the operator can let go of the input at any point in the travel. The worm drive is not, however, the only load-holding feature of the platform. Under a standing machine the load is carried by the locking pawls described below, so that the worm mesh, the sprockets, the endless synchronizing chain 30, and the pinions 20 are relieved of the standing load and are loaded only while the height is being changed.
26	
27	The rotary input may be driven by a removable hand crank 36 received in a crank socket 38 coupled to the worm input shaft 32, as shown in FIG. 4. In another embodiment the hand crank 36 is replaced by a motor coupled to the same worm input shaft 32, the motor acting on the synchronizing transmission through the same worm wheel 34 and producing the same synchronized travel of the four corner posts 16.
28	
29	The endless synchronizing chain 30 running over the front sprocket 26 and the rear sprocket 28 is one form of the synchronizing transmission. In other embodiments the endless synchronizing chain 30 and the sprockets are replaced by a toothed belt running over toothed pulleys fixed to the front transverse shaft 22 and the rear transverse shaft 24, or by a train of gears coupling the front transverse shaft 22 to the rear transverse shaft 24. In each case the transmission constrains all of the pinions 20 to rotate together, and the parallel travel of the equipment deck 12 follows from that constraint rather than from the skill of the operator.
30	
31	Independent load locks at each guided post
32	
33	Referring to FIG. 3, each guide tower 14 carries a locking pawl 40 mounted on a pawl pivot 42 fixed in that guide tower 14. Each locking pawl 40 pivots on its pawl pivot 42 between a locked position, in which a tooth of the locking pawl 40 lies between two teeth of the rack 18 of the corner post 16 that slides in that guide tower 14 and bears on the flank of a rack tooth, and a released position, in which the locking pawl 40 is clear of that rack 18 and the corner post 16 is free to travel. 34	
35	With the four locking pawls 40 in their locked positions, the weight of the equipment deck 12 and of the machine on it passes from each corner post 16 through the engaged locking pawl 40 and its pawl pivot 42 into the guide tower 14 and thence into the base frame 10 and the support surface 64. 36	
37	The tooth pitch of the rack 18 sets the increments at which the locking pawls 40 can engage. Because the four racks 18 are driven through a common synchronizing transmission, the four locking pawls 40 arrive at corresponding positions relative to their respective racks 18, and all four engage teeth at the same height rather than at heights that differ by a pitch from corner to corner.
38	
39	Equalizing release linkage
40	
41	Referring to FIG. 4, a release balance bar 48 is mounted on the base frame 10 on a balance bar pivot 50, and four release cables 46 connect the release balance bar 48 to the four locking pawls 40, one release cable 46 to each locking pawl 40. Each release cable 46 runs from an anchorage on the release balance bar 48 to the locking pawl 40 of one guide tower 14 and is arranged so that tension in the release cable 46 pivots that locking pawl 40 against its compression spring 44 toward the released position. 42	
43	The release handle 52 acts on the release balance bar 48. The release balance bar 48 is pivotable relative to the release handle 52 through a limited angle about the balance bar pivot 50. That freedom is what makes a single-handle release trustworthy at four separate locks. The four release cables 46 are flexible members of finite manufacturing tolerance whose effective lengths change with routing, wear, seating of the cable adjusters 62, and temperature. If the release balance bar 48 were rigidly fixed to the release handle 52, the shortest release cable 46 would lift its locking pawl 40 first and would then absorb the remaining handle travel, and the longest release cable 46 might never develop enough tension to lift its locking pawl 40 at all, leaving one locking pawl 40 engaged with its rack 18 while the other three were released. 44	
45	Releasing the release handle 52 slackens all four release cables 46 and lets each compression spring 44 return its locking pawl 40 into engagement with the nearest tooth of the corresponding rack 18. No further action by the operator is required to lock the platform, and the platform cannot be left unlocked by the omission of a locking step, because locking is the unpowered rest state of every locking pawl 40.
46	
47	Visible confirmation of engagement
48	
49	Each locking pawl 40 carries a locked-state flag 54 that moves with the locking pawl 40, and each guide tower 14 has a window 56 positioned so that the locked-state flag 54 is visible through the window 56 only when that locking pawl 40 is fully engaged with a tooth of the rack 18, as shown in FIG. 3. When the locking pawl 40 is in its released position, or is held short of full engagement because its tooth has landed on the crest of a rack tooth, the locked-state flag 54 is displaced from the window 56 and is not visible. The confirmation is therefore a confirmation of the position of the load-carrying member itself rather than of the position of the release handle 52 or of the release balance bar 48, either of which can be at rest while a locking pawl 40 stands unengaged.
50	
51	The operator confirms that all four locked-state flags 54 are visible through the four windows 56 before removing the hand crank 36 from the crank socket 38 and before the machine on the equipment deck 12 is put into service. 52	
53	Crank and release interlock
54	
55	A mechanical interlock 58 associated with the crank socket 38 couples the crank socket 38 to the release handle 52, as shown in FIG. 4. The mechanical interlock 58 comprises a member that is displaced by the release handle 52 and that lies in the mouth of the crank socket 38 when the release handle 52 is in its rest position, so that the hand crank 36 cannot be inserted into the crank socket 38 unless the release handle 52 is in its pulled position. The same member is captured by the shank of the hand crank 36 while the hand crank 36 is in the crank socket 38, so that the release handle 52 cannot return from its pulled position until the hand crank 36 has been removed from the crank socket 38.
56	
57	The mechanical interlock 58 thereby enforces the order of operations. The platform cannot be driven until the locking pawls 40 have been released, so no locking pawl 40 is dragged along a rack 18 during a height change. The release handle 52 cannot be allowed to return while the drive input is still connected, so the locking pawls 40 are not returned against moving racks 18. Conversely, once the hand crank 36 has been removed, the release handle 52 is free to return, and the operator who has finished the adjustment has nothing left to do that would keep the locking pawls 40 released. The two members the operator handles are thus mutually exclusive by construction, and the failure modes of adjusting with the locks partly engaged and of leaving the platform standing with the locks released are removed rather than merely warned against.
58	
59	Method of use
60	
61	In use, the operator places the base frame 10 on the support surface 64 and mounts the machine on the equipment deck 12. To change the height, the operator pulls and holds the release handle 52, which pivots the release balance bar 48 about the balance bar pivot 50, tensions the four release cables 46, and moves all four locking pawls 40 clear of the four racks 18. With the release handle 52 held in the pulled position, the mechanical interlock 58 clears the mouth of the crank socket 38, and the operator inserts the hand crank 36 into the crank socket 38. The operator turns the hand crank 36, which turns the worm input shaft 32, the worm wheel 34, the front transverse shaft 22, the endless synchronizing chain 30, the rear transverse shaft 24, and the four pinions 20, and so raises or lowers the four corner posts 16 by the same distance, the equipment deck 12 remaining parallel to the base frame 10 throughout the height change.
62	
63	When the desired height of the equipment deck 12 is reached, the operator removes the hand crank 36 from the crank socket 38, which frees the release handle 52, and then releases the release handle 52. The four compression springs 44 return the four locking pawls 40 into engagement with the nearest teeth of the four racks 18. The operator then confirms that the locked-state flag 54 of every locking pawl 40 is visible through the window 56 of the corresponding guide tower 14, and the machine on the equipment deck 12 is thereafter supported through the four engaged locking pawls 40 and the four guide towers 14.
64	
65	Further embodiments
66	
67	The four guide towers 14 near the corners of a rectangular base frame 10 with four corner posts 16 depending from a rectangular equipment deck 12 are one arrangement. In other embodiments the platform has three guide towers 14, or more than four guide towers 14, with one guided post sliding in each guide tower 14 and with one rack 18, one pinion 20, one locking pawl 40 biased by one compression spring 44, one release cable 46, and one locked-state flag 54 at each guided post. The synchronizing transmission then couples the pinions 20 of all of the guide towers 14, and the release balance bar 48 carries one anchorage for each release cable 46 and remains pivotable relative to the release handle 52 so that the same equalization is obtained over the number of locking pawls 40 present. The synchronized drive, the independent locking pawl load locks, the equalizing release balance bar 48, the interlock between the hand crank 36 and the release handle 52, and the visible confirmation of every engaged locking pawl 40 are unchanged by the number of guided posts.
68	
69	The rotary input may be the worm input shaft 32 with the worm wheel 34 turned by the hand crank 36, the same worm input shaft 32 turned by a motor, or the same worm input shaft 32 turned by either at different times, the crank socket 38 remaining available as a manual input.
70	
71	The platform is reusable. It can be lowered, unloaded, moved to another support surface 64, loaded again, and reset to a different height, and the members that carry the standing load, namely the locking pawls 40, the racks 18, the guide towers 14, and the base frame 10, are inspectable through the removable cover 60 and through the windows 56 between uses.
72	
73	The foregoing describes embodiments of the platform. Features described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another embodiment where the two are not mutually exclusive, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims.

With the release handle 52 held in the pulled position, the mechanical interlock 58 clears the mouth of the crank socket 38, and the operator inserts the hand crank 36 into the crank socket 38. The operator turns the hand crank 36, which turns the worm input shaft 32, the worm wheel 34, the front transverse shaft 22, the endless synchronizing chain 30, the rear transverse shaft 24, and the four pinions 20, and so raises or lowers the four corner posts 16 by the same distance, the equipment deck 12 remaining parallel to the base frame 10 throughout the height change.

When the desired height of the equipment deck 12 is reached, the operator removes the hand crank 36 from the crank socket 38, which frees the release handle 52, and then releases the release handle 52. The four compression springs 44 return the four locking pawls 40 into engagement with the nearest teeth of the four racks 18. The operator then confirms that the locked-state flag 54 of every locking pawl 40 is visible through the window 56 of the corresponding guide tower 14, and the machine on the equipment deck 12 is thereafter supported through the four engaged locking pawls 40 and the four guide towers 14.

Further embodiments

The four guide towers 14 near the corners of a rectangular base frame 10 with four corner posts 16 depending from a rectangular equipment deck 12 are one arrangement. In other embodiments the platform has three guide towers 14, or more than four guide towers 14, with one guided post sliding in each guide tower 14 and with one rack 18, one pinion 20, one locking pawl 40 biased by one compression spring 44, one release cable 46, and one locked-state flag 54 at each guided post. The synchronizing transmission then couples the pinions 20 of all of the guide towers 14, and the release balance bar 48 carries one anchorage for each release cable 46 and remains pivotable relative to the release handle 52 so that the same equalization is obtained over the number of locking pawls 40 present. The synchronized drive, the independent locking pawl load locks, the equalizing release balance bar 48, the interlock between the hand crank 36 and the release handle 52, and the visible confirmation of every engaged locking pawl 40 are unchanged by the number of guided posts.

The rotary input may be the worm input shaft 32 with the worm wheel 34 turned by the hand crank 36, the same worm input shaft 32 turned by a motor, or the same worm input shaft 32 turned by either at different times, the crank socket 38 remaining available as a manual input.

The platform is reusable. It can be lowered, unloaded, moved to another support surface 64, loaded again, and reset to a different height, and the members that carry the standing load, namely the locking pawls 40, the racks 18, the guide towers 14, and the base frame 10, are inspectable through the removable cover 60 and through the windows 56 between uses.

The foregoing describes embodiments of the platform. Features described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another embodiment where the two are not mutually exclusive, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims.

input.summary:
Preflight source-fidelity review of p13 (SINGLE-HANDLE SYNCHRONIZED EQUIPMENT PLATFORM WITH INDEPENDENT CORNER LOAD LOCKS), tracing every claim limitation, numbered part, figure-brief statement and description assertion to input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is verbatim identical to the disclosure). There is no further USER correspondence, so the authority is one disclosure text; there are no later USER passages that could add technical matter.

Well-supported core: base frame / equipment deck / four guide towers near the corners / four corner posts sliding vertically; rack on the inward-facing side of each post; a pinion in each tower meshing that rack; front and rear transverse shafts each carrying two pinions; sprockets plus one endless synchronizing chain; hand crank turning a worm input shaft driving a worm wheel fixed to the front shaft; worm resists back-driving but is not the sole load-holder; pivoting locking pawl in each tower with a compression spring biasing it to the locked position; four release cables to a release balance bar mounted on the base frame; release handle that pivots the bar; bar pivotable slightly relative to the handle so cable-length differences do not leave one pawl engaged; springs return pawls to the nearest rack teeth; load through the four engaged pawls and towers; locked-state flag visible through a tower window only at full engagement; interlock on the crank socket both ways; the disclosed method of use; removable cover giving access to worm drive, sprockets, chain, pawls and cable adjusters without removing the deck; and the variants (toothed belt, gear train, motor on the same worm input shaft, three or more than four towers with one rack/pinion/spring-biased pawl/release cable/flag per post). Claims 2-7, 9, 11-13, 15-20 and 22-24, the field, the summary aspects other than the "from outside the platform" phrase, and the abstract (145 words, now within 37 CFR 1.72(b)) trace cleanly. The prior abstract-length gate is cured. Numerals 10-64 are each defined once in numerals.md and each appears on at least one sheet; nothing in numerals.md is orphaned; no placeholders, drafting notes or open questions remain anywhere in draft/ or figures/.

Findings (29). Sixteen are critical untraced technical matter. The largest cluster is functional-surface geometry that the disclosure never describes: FIG. 3 verbalizes the rack as "uniform triangular teeth" with "tooth points directed right", the pawl's "single tooth whose point lies in a valley between two teeth of the rack 18 and rests against the lower flank of the tooth above it", an asymmetric "narrow clearance" on one side of the post against a "wider open gap" on the other, the spring seated on the wall band "below the pawl pivot 42", the flag "above the pawl pivot 42 ... reaching into the thickness of the right wall band", and the pivot on "a short bracket joining the inner face of the right wall band". Under the stated convention rule these are contact topology, which flank bears, and radial/axial end positions on functional faces, so they are substantive even though FIG. 3 is fragmentary; the disclosure says only that the pawl "pivots between a locked position engaging the rack" and is "fully engaged with a rack tooth". The description repeats part of it ("bears on the flank of a rack tooth"). FIG. 4 likewise verbalizes a socket "open mouth facing downward and its closed end upward" and a two-left/two-right anchorage split on the balance bar, both of which carry function.

The other critical items are invention statements with no source passage at all: deck mounting "through mounting holes, rails, or clamps"; tower "bearing surfaces at the upper and lower ends" taking "the horizontal reactions produced by an off-centre machine"; the inward-rack advantage of being "shielded from weather and from impact"; placing the release handle and crank "at the same side"; the asserted result that all four pawls "engage teeth at the same height rather than at heights that differ by a pitch"; the crest-landing condition (also dependent claim 8); the corrective "turn the crank to the next tooth position" step (also claim 21); the specific interlock member "in the mouth of the crank socket" "captured by the shank" (also claim 10 and FIG. 4); the crank-or-motor-at-different-times hybrid; "confirmed from outside the platform"; and extending cover/window inspection to "the racks 18, the guide towers 14, and the base frame 10".

Seven major findings: equal sprocket tooth counts and equal rack pitch stated as structure; "high-reduction mesh"; the claim 14 spring-seating limitation; numeral 50 used with two different meanings (a mount of the bar to the base frame in the description versus the bar-to-handle relative joint in FIG. 4) together with FIG. 4 omitting the base-frame mounting that claims 1 and 17 require; claims 1 and 19 reciting "a plurality of" guide towers, which reads on two when the disclosure's floor is three; FIG. 2 asserting pinion teeth "touch" four unnumbered corner blocks with no rack 18 anywhere on the sheet; and the untraced cable-length drivers "routing, wear, seating of the cable adjusters 62, and temperature".

Six minor findings cover FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 proportion and placement verbalizations that go past a generic outline, the "housed in the base frame" versus "mounted in each guide tower" tension for the pinions, FIG. 3 being a sectional view with no section line indicated on any source view, FIG. 1 showing the crank installed without the pulled handle its own interlock requires, and claim 13 listing the release cables among what the cover closes.

Every finding carries the candidate quotation, the nearest source passage showing the gap, and a delete-or-conform fix that leaves filing-clean text. No image files were inspected.

findings.title: Deck mounting means (mounting holes, rails, clamps) have no source support
findings.detail: The description specifies structures by which the machine is attached to the deck. The disclosure says only that the operator "mounts the equipment on the deck" and never describes any mounting interface, let alone holes, rails or clamps, or their location at the upper face.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The equipment deck 12 receives the machine it supports, for example through mounting holes, rails, or clamps at the upper face of the equipment deck 12". Nearest source (disclosure.md): "mounts the equipment on the deck" and "The equipment deck carries four corner posts" - no affirmative passage discloses any mounting feature on the deck.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The equipment deck 12 receives the machine it supports, and the machine remains on the equipment deck 12 while the height of the equipment deck 12 is changed."

findings.title: Guide tower internal geometry and bearing surfaces are untraced
findings.detail: The description asserts a hollow interior matched to the post cross section, bearing surfaces at the upper and lower ends of that interior, and a stated load function (horizontal reactions from an off-centre machine). The disclosure discloses only that the posts "slide vertically in the respective guide towers". Nothing discloses interior fit, discrete bearing surfaces, their end locations, or off-centre loading.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Each guide tower 14 is a hollow upright member whose interior corresponds to the cross section of the corner post 16 that slides in it, and bearing surfaces at the upper and lower ends of the interior of the guide tower 14 take the horizontal reactions produced by an off-centre machine on the equipment deck 12." Nearest source: "The equipment deck carries four corner posts that slide vertically in the respective guide towers." - no affirmative passage on tower interiors or bearing surfaces.
findings.fix: Delete the quoted sentence. Retain only the preceding sentence, ending: "...so that each corner post 16 slides vertically in a respective one of the guide towers 14."

findings.title: Asserted advantages of the inward-facing rack (weather and impact shielding, operator reach) are untraced
findings.detail: The description asserts results and operating conditions for the disclosed inward-facing rack position that the disclosure never states: containment inside the platform footprint, shielding from weather and impact, and operator access to the drive members from within the base frame.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Placing the rack 18 on the inward-facing side keeps the toothed face of the rack 18 and the members that engage it inside the footprint of the platform, where they are shielded from weather and from impact, and lets an operator reach the drive members of all four guide towers 14 from within the base frame 10." Nearest source: "Each corner post has a rack along an inward-facing side." - the disclosure gives the position and no advantage of it.
findings.fix: Delete the quoted sentence, leaving: "In the illustrated embodiment the rack 18 lies along an inward-facing side of the corner post 16, that is, the side of the corner post 16 that faces the interior of the base frame 10."

findings.title: Relative placement of the release handle and hand crank on the same side of the base frame is untraced
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, last paragraph of "Overall arrangement"; figures/fig-01.md, "Structures and relationships"
findings.detail: The application text verbalizes a positional relationship between the two operator members (same side of the frame, reachable by an operator standing beside the platform) and the figure brief fixes them on the front wall to the left and right of the cover. The disclosure places neither the handle nor the crank socket anywhere on the platform. This is a relative-location statement conveying technical substance, not a page-placement convention.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "A release handle 52 projects from the base frame 10 where an operator standing beside the platform can reach it, and a hand crank 36 is inserted into the base frame 10 at the same side to drive the platform." Candidate (fig-01): "A release handle 52 ... projecting forward and slightly upward from the front wall of the base frame 10, left of the removable cover 60"; "A hand crank 36 is drawn right of the removable cover 60 as a short horizontal shaft entering the front wall of the base frame 10". Nearest source: "A release handle pivots the balance bar" and "A removable hand crank turns a worm input shaft" - no location is disclosed for either.
findings.fix: In the description, replace the quoted sentence with: "A release handle 52 and a hand crank 36 are the members the operator handles, and the sequence in which they may be handled is enforced mechanically, as described below." In fig-01.md, delete "left of the removable cover 60" and "right of the removable cover 60" and state each member only as projecting from a wall of the base frame 10, shown schematically.

findings.title: Pawl-to-rack contact topology (tooth in a valley, bearing on the lower flank of the tooth above) is untraced
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, first paragraph of "Independent load locks at each guided post"; figures/fig-03.md, "Structures and relationships"
findings.detail: Both the description and the figure brief specify which surfaces contact and which flank carries load: a single pawl tooth entering a valley between two rack teeth and bearing on the lower flank of the tooth above. Under the governing convention rule, contact topology and which flank bears are substantive even in a fragmentary section. The disclosure states only that the pawl engages the rack and is fully engaged with a rack tooth.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "a locked position, in which a tooth of the locking pawl 40 lies between two teeth of the rack 18 and bears on the flank of a rack tooth". Candidate (fig-03): "Its left end is a single tooth whose point lies in a valley between two teeth of the rack 18 and rests against the lower flank of the tooth above it. The body widens from that tooth toward the right." Nearest source: "a locking pawl that pivots between a locked position engaging the rack of its corner post and a released position clear of the rack"; "fully engaged with a rack tooth". No affirmative passage describes pawl tooth count, valley entry, or which flank bears.
findings.fix: In the description, replace with: "a locked position, in which the locking pawl 40 engages the rack 18 of the corner post 16 that slides in that guide tower 14, and a released position, in which the locking pawl 40 is clear of that rack 18 and the corner post 16 is free to travel." In fig-03.md, replace the quoted sentences with: "A locking pawl 40 is a solid unhatched body in the gap at mid height, its left end engaging the rack 18, shown schematically."

findings.title: Rack tooth profile and tooth-point direction in FIG. 3 are untraced
findings.detail: The brief verbalizes the tooth profile (uniform triangular), the pitch condition, and the direction in which the tooth points run out. Tooth profile, taper and runout direction on a functional toothed face are substantive under the governing rule. The disclosure discloses a rack and rack teeth but no profile, no flank angle, and no runout direction.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A rack 18 is a row of uniform triangular teeth of constant pitch along the right side of the corner post 16, the tooth points directed right into the wider gap, the row running the full sectioned length of that column." Nearest source: "Each corner post has a rack along an inward-facing side" and "into engagement with the nearest rack teeth" - no tooth geometry is disclosed.
findings.fix: Replace with: "A rack 18 is a row of teeth of constant pitch along one side of the corner post 16, the row running the full sectioned length of that column, the teeth shown schematically."

findings.title: Asymmetric clearance between the corner post and the two tower wall bands is untraced
findings.detail: The brief asserts a narrow clearance on one side of the post and a deliberately wider gap on the other, which is the space the pawl, spring and flag occupy. This is a relative-location and proportion statement that carries technical function (it creates the pawl pocket). The disclosure says only that the post slides in the tower and that the tower carries the pawl.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Its left side lies close to the inner face of the left wall band with a narrow clearance. A wider open gap is left between its right side and the inner face of the right wall band." Nearest source: "Each guide tower also carries a locking pawl"; "four corner posts that slide vertically in the respective guide towers" - no passage discloses clearances or an asymmetric pocket.
findings.fix: Replace both sentences with: "A corner post 16 appears in section as an upright hatched column between the two wall bands, spaced from each of them, the space on the rack side accommodating the locking pawl 40, shown schematically."

findings.title: Spring, pivot-bracket and flag positions relative to the pawl pivot in FIG. 3 are untraced
findings.detail: The brief fixes the spring below the pivot with named seating faces, the pivot on a bracket joining a named wall band, and the flag above the pivot projecting into the wall thickness. Which side of a pivot a biasing spring acts on determines the sense of the bias torque, and the flag's end position determines what appears in the window; both are substantive. None of it is disclosed.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A compression spring 44 is a coiled line in the wider gap below the pawl pivot 42, its right end seated against the inner face of the right wall band and its left end against the lower right portion of that body." "A pawl pivot 42 is a small circle with a centre mark in the right-hand part of that body, carried by a short bracket joining the inner face of the right wall band". "A locked-state flag 54 is a small tab projecting right from the upper part of that body, above the pawl pivot 42, its right end reaching into the thickness of the right wall band." Nearest source: "A compression spring biases each locking pawl toward the locked position"; "Each locking pawl carries a locked-state flag that is visible through a window in the corresponding guide tower only when that pawl is fully engaged with a rack tooth." No bracket, no above/below relationship, and no seating faces are disclosed.
findings.fix: Replace with: "A pawl pivot 42 is a small circle with a centre mark in that body, mounted to the guide tower 14, shown schematically. A compression spring 44 is a coiled line acting between the guide tower 14 and that body so as to bias the locking pawl 40 toward the locked position, shown schematically. A locked-state flag 54 is a small tab carried by that body and aligned with the window 56, shown schematically."

findings.title: Asserted result that all four pawls engage rack teeth at the same height is untraced
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, last paragraph of "Independent load locks at each guided post"
findings.detail: The description asserts a specific engagement result (corresponding pawl positions and equal engagement heights, versus heights differing by one pitch corner to corner). The disclosure states that all posts move the same distance and that the springs return the pawls to the nearest rack teeth, but never asserts that the four engagement heights coincide or discusses pitch-level differences between corners.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Because the four racks 18 are driven through a common synchronizing transmission, the four locking pawls 40 arrive at corresponding positions relative to their respective racks 18, and all four engage teeth at the same height rather than at heights that differ by a pitch from corner to corner." Nearest source: "Releasing the handle lets the four pawl springs return the pawls into engagement with the nearest rack teeth."
findings.fix: Delete the quoted sentence, leaving: "The tooth pitch of the rack 18 sets the increments at which the locking pawls 40 can engage."

findings.title: Crest-landing condition (pawl held short of engagement by a rack tooth crest) is untraced, in the description and in claim 8
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Visible confirmation of engagement", first paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 8
findings.detail: A specific partial-engagement condition is recited as a structural/operating condition and is the entire subject of dependent claim 8. The disclosure states only that the flag is visible only when the pawl is fully engaged with a rack tooth; it never describes a pawl landing on a tooth crest.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "or is held short of full engagement because its tooth has landed on the crest of a rack tooth, the locked-state flag 54 is displaced from the window 56 and is not visible". Candidate (claim 8): "wherein the locked-state flag is displaced from the window and is not visible through the window when the locking pawl is in the released position and when the locking pawl is held short of full engagement by a crest of a tooth of the rack." Nearest source: "a locked-state flag that is visible through a window in the corresponding guide tower only when that pawl is fully engaged with a rack tooth".
findings.fix: In the description, replace with: "When the locking pawl 40 is not fully engaged with a tooth of the rack 18, the locked-state flag 54 is displaced from the window 56 and is not visible." Cancel claim 8 and renumber claims 9-15 as 8-14, updating the dependency in present claim 8's place accordingly (no other claim depends on claim 8).

findings.title: Corrective procedure of cranking to the next tooth position is untraced, in the description and in claim 21
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Visible confirmation of engagement", second paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 21
findings.detail: A remedial method step is described and claimed: on seeing a flag absent, the operator turns the crank a small amount to move the posts to the next tooth position so the springs seat all pawls. The disclosure's use sequence ends with confirming the four flags and contains no corrective action.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "the operator restores engagement by turning the hand crank 36 a small amount so that the corner posts 16 move to the next tooth position and the compression springs 44 seat all four locking pawls 40." Candidate (claim 21): "further comprising, when the locked-state flag of one of the locking pawls is not visible ... turning the rotary input so that the posts move to a next tooth position and the springs seat all of the locking pawls." Nearest source: "removes the hand crank, releases the handle, and confirms that all four locked-state flags are visible."
findings.fix: In the description, end the sentence at: "A locked-state flag 54 that is not visible tells the operator, at the guide tower 14 concerned, that the locking pawl 40 there has not seated." Cancel claim 21 and renumber the following claims (no claim depends on claim 21).

findings.title: Specific interlock mechanism (member in the socket mouth, captured by the crank shank) is untraced, in the description, claim 10 and FIG. 4
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Crank and release interlock", first paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 10; figures/fig-04.md
findings.detail: The disclosure discloses only the interlock's two blocking functions. The candidate adds an implementing structure: a member displaced by the handle that lies in the mouth of the crank socket and is captured by the shank of the crank, plus a link line joining that member to the handle below the balance bar pivot. No source passage describes any interlock structure.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "The mechanical interlock 58 comprises a member that is displaced by the release handle 52 and that lies in the mouth of the crank socket 38 when the release handle 52 is in its rest position ... The same member is captured by the shank of the hand crank 36 while the hand crank 36 is in the crank socket 38". Candidate (claim 10): "the mechanical interlock comprises a member displaced by the release handle, the member lying in a mouth of the crank socket ... and being captured by a shank of the hand crank". Candidate (fig-04): "A mechanical interlock 58 is a small bar lying across the open mouth of the crank socket 38, together with a straight link line joining that small bar to the release handle 52 below the balance bar pivot 50". Nearest source: "A mechanical interlock on the crank socket blocks insertion of the hand crank unless the release handle is in its pulled position, and blocks return of the release handle until the crank is removed."
findings.fix: In the description, replace the quoted sentences with: "The mechanical interlock 58 blocks insertion of the hand crank 36 into the crank socket 38 unless the release handle 52 is in its pulled position, and blocks return of the release handle 52 from its pulled position until the hand crank 36 has been removed from the crank socket 38." Cancel claim 10 and renumber the following claims. In fig-04.md, replace with: "A mechanical interlock 58 is drawn at the crank socket 38 and coupled to the release handle 52, shown schematically."

findings.title: Hybrid crank-or-motor-at-different-times embodiment is untraced
findings.detail: The disclosed variant is a substitution: the hand crank is replaced by a motor acting on the same worm input shaft. The candidate adds a further embodiment in which both drive the same shaft at different times with the crank socket retained as a manual input. No source passage discloses a dual-input platform.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "or the same worm input shaft 32 turned by either at different times, the crank socket 38 remaining available as a manual input." Nearest source: "the hand crank is replaced by a motor acting on the same worm input shaft".
findings.fix: End the paragraph after the disclosed alternatives: "The rotary input may be the worm input shaft 32 with the worm wheel 34 turned by the hand crank 36, or the same worm input shaft 32 turned by a motor."

findings.title: "Confirmed from outside the platform" is untraced and conflicts with the window location shown
findings.detail: The summary asserts a viewing location for the flag confirmation. The disclosure says only that the flag is visible through a window in the guide tower. The added phrase is also in tension with FIG. 3, where the window is in the wall band on the rack side, i.e. the tower wall facing the interior of the base frame per the inward-facing rack.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "so that the state of every load lock can be confirmed from outside the platform before the platform is loaded." Nearest source: "Each locking pawl carries a locked-state flag that is visible through a window in the corresponding guide tower only when that pawl is fully engaged with a rack tooth. The operator must see all four flags before removing the hand crank or loading the deck."

findings.title: Two-left / two-right anchorage split of the release cables on the balance bar is untraced
findings.detail: The brief fixes the circumferential distribution of the four cable anchorages about the balance bar pivot (two on each side) and asserts non-crossing routing. Anchorage positions on each side of the pivot are what produce the equalizing moment balance, so this is substantive topology, not page placement. The disclosure discloses four cables to the bar and slight pivoting, with no anchorage arrangement.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Each path begins at one of four anchor points spaced along the release balance bar 48, two of them left of the balance bar pivot 50 and two of them right of it, and runs outward and away from the release balance bar 48 to end at one of the four blocks. The four paths do not cross one another." Nearest source: "The four locking pawls are connected by four release cables to a release balance bar mounted on the base frame." The description likewise says only "an anchorage on the release balance bar 48".
findings.fix: Replace with: "Each path begins at one of four anchor points on the release balance bar 48 and runs outward to one of the four blocks, shown schematically."

findings.title: Crank socket open-mouth orientation and closed end in FIG. 4 are untraced
findings.detail: The brief states which end of the socket is open and which is closed and the direction the mouth faces. Under the governing rule, statements about which end of a functional slot or port is open or deeper and its end orientation are substantive even where the geometry is called schematic. The disclosure discloses a crank socket only as the thing the interlock acts on.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A crank socket 38 is drawn to the right of the release handle 52 in the lower part of the drawing area as a short open-ended sleeve seen from the side, its open mouth facing downward and its closed end upward, shown schematically." Preflight source-fidelity review of p13 (SINGLE-HANDLE SYNCHRONIZED EQUIPMENT PLATFORM WITH INDEPENDENT CORNER LOAD LOCKS), tracing every claim limitation, numbered part, figure-brief statement and description assertion to input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is verbatim identical to the disclosure). There is no further USER correspondence, so the authority is one disclosure text; there are no later USER passages that could add technical matter.

Well-supported core: base frame / equipment deck / four guide towers near the corners / four corner posts sliding vertically; rack on the inward-facing side of each post; a pinion in each tower meshing that rack; front and rear transverse shafts each carrying two pinions; sprockets plus one endless synchronizing chain; hand crank turning a worm input shaft driving a worm wheel fixed to the front shaft; worm resists back-driving but is not the sole load-holder; pivoting locking pawl in each tower with a compression spring biasing it to the locked position; four release cables to a release balance bar mounted on the base frame; release handle that pivots the bar; bar pivotable slightly relative to the handle so cable-length differences do not leave one pawl engaged; springs return pawls to the nearest rack teeth; load through the four engaged pawls and towers; locked-state flag visible through a tower window only at full engagement; interlock on the crank socket both ways; the disclosed method of use; removable cover giving access to worm drive, sprockets, chain, pawls and cable adjusters without removing the deck; and the variants (toothed belt, gear train, motor on the same worm input shaft, three or more than four towers with one rack/pinion/spring-biased pawl/release cable/flag per post). Claims 2-7, 9, 11-13, 15-20 and 22-24, the field, the summary aspects other than the "from outside the platform" phrase, and the abstract (145 words, now within 37 CFR 1.72(b)) trace cleanly. The prior abstract-length gate is cured. Numerals 10-64 are each defined once in numerals.md and each appears on at least one sheet; nothing in numerals.md is orphaned; no placeholders, drafting notes or open questions remain anywhere in draft/ or figures/.

Findings (29). Sixteen are critical untraced technical matter. The largest cluster is functional-surface geometry that the disclosure never describes: FIG. 3 verbalizes the rack as "uniform triangular teeth" with "tooth points directed right", the pawl's "single tooth whose point lies in a valley between two teeth of the rack 18 and rests against the lower flank of the tooth above it", an asymmetric "narrow clearance" on one side of the post against a "wider open gap" on the other, the spring seated on the wall band "below the pawl pivot 42", the flag "above the pawl pivot 42 ... reaching into the thickness of the right wall band", and the pivot on "a short bracket joining the inner face of the right wall band". Under the stated convention rule these are contact topology, which flank bears, and radial/axial end positions on functional faces, so they are substantive even though FIG. 3 is fragmentary; the disclosure says only that the pawl "pivots between a locked position engaging the rack" and is "fully engaged with a rack tooth". The description repeats part of it ("bears on the flank of a rack tooth"). FIG. 4 likewise verbalizes a socket "open mouth facing downward and its closed end upward" and a two-left/two-right anchorage split on the balance bar, both of which carry function.

The other critical items are invention statements with no source passage at all: deck mounting "through mounting holes, rails, or clamps"; tower "bearing surfaces at the upper and lower ends" taking "the horizontal reactions produced by an off-centre machine"; the inward-rack advantage of being "shielded from weather and from impact"; placing the release handle and crank "at the same side"; the asserted result that all four pawls "engage teeth at the same height rather than at heights that differ by a pitch"; the crest-landing condition (also dependent claim 8); the corrective "turn the crank to the next tooth position" step (also claim 21); the specific interlock member "in the mouth of the crank socket" "captured by the shank" (also claim 10 and FIG. 4); the crank-or-motor-at-different-times hybrid; "confirmed from outside the platform"; and extending cover/window inspection to "the racks 18, the guide towers 14, and the base frame 10".

Seven major findings: equal sprocket tooth counts and equal rack pitch stated as structure; "high-reduction mesh"; the claim 14 spring-seating limitation; numeral 50 used with two different meanings (a mount of the bar to the base frame in the description versus the bar-to-handle relative joint in FIG. 4) together with FIG. 4 omitting the base-frame mounting that claims 1 and 17 require; claims 1 and 19 reciting "a plurality of" guide towers, which reads on two when the disclosure's floor is three; FIG. 2 asserting pinion teeth "touch" four unnumbered corner blocks with no rack 18 anywhere on the sheet; and the untraced cable-length drivers "routing, wear, seating of the cable adjusters 62, and temperature".

Six minor findings cover FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 proportion and placement verbalizations that go past a generic outline, the "housed in the base frame" versus "mounted in each guide tower" tension for the pinions, FIG. 3 being a sectional view with no section line indicated on any source view, FIG. 1 showing the crank installed without the pulled handle its own interlock requires, and claim 13 listing the release cables among what the cover closes.

Every finding carries the candidate quotation, the nearest source passage showing the gap, and a delete-or-conform fix that leaves filing-clean text. No image files were inspected.
