findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The equipment deck 12 receives the machine it supports, and the machine remains on the equipment deck 12 while the height of the equipment deck 12 is changed."

findings.title: Guide tower internal geometry and bearing surfaces are untraced
findings.detail: The description asserts a hollow interior matched to the post cross section, bearing surfaces at the upper and lower ends of that interior, and a stated load function (horizontal reactions from an off-centre machine). The disclosure discloses only that the posts "slide vertically in the respective guide towers". Nothing discloses interior fit, discrete bearing surfaces, their end locations, or off-centre loading.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Each guide tower 14 is a hollow upright member whose interior corresponds to the cross section of the corner post 16 that slides in it, and bearing surfaces at the upper and lower ends of the interior of the guide tower 14 take the horizontal reactions produced by an off-centre machine on the equipment deck 12." Nearest source: "The equipment deck carries four corner posts that slide vertically in the respective guide towers." - no affirmative passage on tower interiors or bearing surfaces.
findings.fix: Delete the quoted sentence. Retain only the preceding sentence, ending: "...so that each corner post 16 slides vertically in a respective one of the guide towers 14."

findings.title: Asserted advantages of the inward-facing rack (weather and impact shielding, operator reach) are untraced
findings.detail: The description asserts results and operating conditions for the disclosed inward-facing rack position that the disclosure never states: containment inside the platform footprint, shielding from weather and impact, and operator access to the drive members from within the base frame.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Placing the rack 18 on the inward-facing side keeps the toothed face of the rack 18 and the members that engage it inside the footprint of the platform, where they are shielded from weather and from impact, and lets an operator reach the drive members of all four guide towers 14 from within the base frame 10." Nearest source: "Each corner post has a rack along an inward-facing side." - the disclosure gives the position and no advantage of it.
findings.fix: Delete the quoted sentence, leaving: "In the illustrated embodiment the rack 18 lies along an inward-facing side of the corner post 16, that is, the side of the corner post 16 that faces the interior of the base frame 10."

findings.title: Relative placement of the release handle and hand crank on the same side of the base frame is untraced
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, last paragraph of "Overall arrangement"; figures/fig-01.md, "Structures and relationships"
findings.detail: The application text verbalizes a positional relationship between the two operator members (same side of the frame, reachable by an operator standing beside the platform) and the figure brief fixes them on the front wall to the left and right of the cover. The disclosure places neither the handle nor the crank socket anywhere on the platform. This is a relative-location statement conveying technical substance, not a page-placement convention.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "A release handle 52 projects from the base frame 10 where an operator standing beside the platform can reach it, and a hand crank 36 is inserted into the base frame 10 at the same side to drive the platform." Candidate (fig-01): "A release handle 52 ... projecting forward and slightly upward from the front wall of the base frame 10, left of the removable cover 60"; "A hand crank 36 is drawn right of the removable cover 60 as a short horizontal shaft entering the front wall of the base frame 10". Nearest source: "A release handle pivots the balance bar" and "A removable hand crank turns a worm input shaft" - no location is disclosed for either.
findings.fix: In the description, replace the quoted sentence with: "A release handle 52 and a hand crank 36 are the members the operator handles, and the sequence in which they may be handled is enforced mechanically, as described below." In fig-01.md, delete "left of the removable cover 60" and "right of the removable cover 60" and state each member only as projecting from a wall of the base frame 10, shown schematically.

findings.title: Pawl-to-rack contact topology (tooth in a valley, bearing on the lower flank of the tooth above) is untraced
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, first paragraph of "Independent load locks at each guided post"; figures/fig-03.md, "Structures and relationships"
findings.detail: Both the description and the figure brief specify which surfaces contact and which flank carries load: a single pawl tooth entering a valley between two rack teeth and bearing on the lower flank of the tooth above. Under the governing convention rule, contact topology and which flank bears are substantive even in a fragmentary section. The disclosure states only that the pawl engages the rack and is fully engaged with a rack tooth.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "a locked position, in which a tooth of the locking pawl 40 lies between two teeth of the rack 18 and bears on the flank of a rack tooth". Candidate (fig-03): "Its left end is a single tooth whose point lies in a valley between two teeth of the rack 18 and rests against the lower flank of the tooth above it. The body widens from that tooth toward the right." Nearest source: "a locking pawl that pivots between a locked position engaging the rack of its corner post and a released position clear of the rack"; "fully engaged with a rack tooth". No affirmative passage describes pawl tooth count, valley entry, or which flank bears.
findings.fix: In the description, replace with: "a locked position, in which the locking pawl 40 engages the rack 18 of the corner post 16 that slides in that guide tower 14, and a released position, in which the locking pawl 40 is clear of that rack 18 and the corner post 16 is free to travel." In fig-03.md, replace the quoted sentences with: "A locking pawl 40 is a solid unhatched body in the gap at mid height, its left end engaging the rack 18, shown schematically."

findings.title: Rack tooth profile and tooth-point direction in FIG. 3 are untraced
findings.detail: The brief verbalizes the tooth profile (uniform triangular), the pitch condition, and the direction in which the tooth points run out. Tooth profile, taper and runout direction on a functional toothed face are substantive under the governing rule. The disclosure discloses a rack and rack teeth but no profile, no flank angle, and no runout direction.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A rack 18 is a row of uniform triangular teeth of constant pitch along the right side of the corner post 16, the tooth points directed right into the wider gap, the row running the full sectioned length of that column." Nearest source: "Each corner post has a rack along an inward-facing side" and "into engagement with the nearest rack teeth" - no tooth geometry is disclosed.
findings.fix: Replace with: "A rack 18 is a row of teeth of constant pitch along one side of the corner post 16, the row running the full sectioned length of that column, the teeth shown schematically."

findings.title: Asymmetric clearance between the corner post and the two tower wall bands is untraced
findings.detail: The brief asserts a narrow clearance on one side of the post and a deliberately wider gap on the other, which is the space the pawl, spring and flag occupy. This is a relative-location and proportion statement that carries technical function (it creates the pawl pocket). The disclosure says only that the post slides in the tower and that the tower carries the pawl.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Its left side lies close to the inner face of the left wall band with a narrow clearance. A wider open gap is left between its right side and the inner face of the right wall band." Nearest source: "Each guide tower also carries a locking pawl"; "four corner posts that slide vertically in the respective guide towers" - no passage discloses clearances or an asymmetric pocket.
findings.fix: Replace both sentences with: "A corner post 16 appears in section as an upright hatched column between the two wall bands, spaced from each of them, the space on the rack side accommodating the locking pawl 40, shown schematically."

findings.title: Spring, pivot-bracket and flag positions relative to the pawl pivot in FIG. 3 are untraced
findings.detail: The brief fixes the spring below the pivot with named seating faces, the pivot on a bracket joining a named wall band, and the flag above the pivot projecting into the wall thickness. Which side of a pivot a biasing spring acts on determines the sense of the bias torque, and the flag's end position determines what appears in the window; both are substantive. None of it is disclosed.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A compression spring 44 is a coiled line in the wider gap below the pawl pivot 42, its right end seated against the inner face of the right wall band and its left end against the lower right portion of that body." "A pawl pivot 42 is a small circle with a centre mark in the right-hand part of that body, carried by a short bracket joining the inner face of the right wall band". "A locked-state flag 54 is a small tab projecting right from the upper part of that body, above the pawl pivot 42, its right end reaching into the thickness of the right wall band." Nearest source: "A compression spring biases each locking pawl toward the locked position"; "Each locking pawl carries a locked-state flag that is visible through a window in the corresponding guide tower only when that pawl is fully engaged with a rack tooth." No bracket, no above/below relationship, and no seating faces are disclosed.
findings.fix: Replace with: "A pawl pivot 42 is a small circle with a centre mark in that body, mounted to the guide tower 14, shown schematically. A compression spring 44 is a coiled line acting between the guide tower 14 and that body so as to bias the locking pawl 40 toward the locked position, shown schematically. A locked-state flag 54 is a small tab carried by that body and aligned with the window 56, shown schematically."

findings.title: Asserted result that all four pawls engage rack teeth at the same height is untraced
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, last paragraph of "Independent load locks at each guided post"
findings.detail: The description asserts a specific engagement result (corresponding pawl positions and equal engagement heights, versus heights differing by one pitch corner to corner). The disclosure states that all posts move the same distance and that the springs return the pawls to the nearest rack teeth, but never asserts that the four engagement heights coincide or discusses pitch-level differences between corners.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Because the four racks 18 are driven through a common synchronizing transmission, the four locking pawls 40 arrive at corresponding positions relative to their respective racks 18, and all four engage teeth at the same height rather than at heights that differ by a pitch from corner to corner." Nearest source: "Releasing the handle lets the four pawl springs return the pawls into engagement with the nearest rack teeth."
findings.fix: Delete the quoted sentence, leaving: "The tooth pitch of the rack 18 sets the increments at which the locking pawls 40 can engage."

findings.title: Crest-landing condition (pawl held short of engagement by a rack tooth crest) is untraced, in the description and in claim 8
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Visible confirmation of engagement", first paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 8
findings.detail: A specific partial-engagement condition is recited as a structural/operating condition and is the entire subject of dependent claim 8. The disclosure states only that the flag is visible only when the pawl is fully engaged with a rack tooth; it never describes a pawl landing on a tooth crest.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "or is held short of full engagement because its tooth has landed on the crest of a rack tooth, the locked-state flag 54 is displaced from the window 56 and is not visible". Candidate (claim 8): "wherein the locked-state flag is displaced from the window and is not visible through the window when the locking pawl is in the released position and when the locking pawl is held short of full engagement by a crest of a tooth of the rack." Nearest source: "a locked-state flag that is visible through a window in the corresponding guide tower only when that pawl is fully engaged with a rack tooth".
findings.fix: In the description, replace with: "When the locking pawl 40 is not fully engaged with a tooth of the rack 18, the locked-state flag 54 is displaced from the window 56 and is not visible." Cancel claim 8 and renumber claims 9-15 as 8-14, updating the dependency in present claim 8's place accordingly (no other claim depends on claim 8).

findings.title: Corrective procedure of cranking to the next tooth position is untraced, in the description and in claim 21
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Visible confirmation of engagement", second paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 21
findings.detail: A remedial method step is described and claimed: on seeing a flag absent, the operator turns the crank a small amount to move the posts to the next tooth position so the springs seat all pawls. The disclosure's use sequence ends with confirming the four flags and contains no corrective action.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "the operator restores engagement by turning the hand crank 36 a small amount so that the corner posts 16 move to the next tooth position and the compression springs 44 seat all four locking pawls 40." Candidate (claim 21): "further comprising, when the locked-state flag of one of the locking pawls is not visible ... turning the rotary input so that the posts move to a next tooth position and the springs seat all of the locking pawls." Nearest source: "removes the hand crank, releases the handle, and confirms that all four locked-state flags are visible."
findings.fix: In the description, end the sentence at: "A locked-state flag 54 that is not visible tells the operator, at the guide tower 14 concerned, that the locking pawl 40 there has not seated." Cancel claim 21 and renumber the following claims (no claim depends on claim 21).

findings.title: Specific interlock mechanism (member in the socket mouth, captured by the crank shank) is untraced, in the description, claim 10 and FIG. 4
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Crank and release interlock", first paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 10; figures/fig-04.md
findings.detail: The disclosure discloses only the interlock's two blocking functions. The candidate adds an implementing structure: a member displaced by the handle that lies in the mouth of the crank socket and is captured by the shank of the crank, plus a link line joining that member to the handle below the balance bar pivot. No source passage describes any interlock structure.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "The mechanical interlock 58 comprises a member that is displaced by the release handle 52 and that lies in the mouth of the crank socket 38 when the release handle 52 is in its rest position ... The same member is captured by the shank of the hand crank 36 while the hand crank 36 is in the crank socket 38". Candidate (claim 10): "the mechanical interlock comprises a member displaced by the release handle, the member lying in a mouth of the crank socket ... and being captured by a shank of the hand crank". Candidate (fig-04): "A mechanical interlock 58 is a small bar lying across the open mouth of the crank socket 38, together with a straight link line joining that small bar to the release handle 52 below the balance bar pivot 50". Nearest source: "A mechanical interlock on the crank socket blocks insertion of the hand crank unless the release handle is in its pulled position, and blocks return of the release handle until the crank is removed."
findings.fix: In the description, replace the quoted sentences with: "The mechanical interlock 58 blocks insertion of the hand crank 36 into the crank socket 38 unless the release handle 52 is in its pulled position, and blocks return of the release handle 52 from its pulled position until the hand crank 36 has been removed from the crank socket 38." Cancel claim 10 and renumber the following claims. In fig-04.md, replace with: "A mechanical interlock 58 is drawn at the crank socket 38 and coupled to the release handle 52, shown schematically."

findings.title: Hybrid crank-or-motor-at-different-times embodiment is untraced
findings.detail: The disclosed variant is a substitution: the hand crank is replaced by a motor acting on the same worm input shaft. The candidate adds a further embodiment in which both drive the same shaft at different times with the crank socket retained as a manual input. No source passage discloses a dual-input platform.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "or the same worm input shaft 32 turned by either at different times, the crank socket 38 remaining available as a manual input." Nearest source: "the hand crank is replaced by a motor acting on the same worm input shaft".
findings.fix: End the paragraph after the disclosed alternatives: "The rotary input may be the worm input shaft 32 with the worm wheel 34 turned by the hand crank 36, or the same worm input shaft 32 turned by a motor."

findings.title: "Confirmed from outside the platform" is untraced and conflicts with the window location shown
findings.detail: The summary asserts a viewing location for the flag confirmation. The disclosure says only that the flag is visible through a window in the guide tower. The added phrase is also in tension with FIG. 3, where the window is in the wall band on the rack side, i.e. the tower wall facing the interior of the base frame per the inward-facing rack.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "so that the state of every load lock can be confirmed from outside the platform before the platform is loaded." Nearest source: "Each locking pawl carries a locked-state flag that is visible through a window in the corresponding guide tower only when that pawl is fully engaged with a rack tooth. The operator must see all four flags before removing the hand crank or loading the deck."
findings.fix: Replace with: "so that the state of every load lock can be confirmed before the platform is loaded."

findings.title: Two-left / two-right anchorage split of the release cables on the balance bar is untraced
findings.detail: The brief fixes the circumferential distribution of the four cable anchorages about the balance bar pivot (two on each side) and asserts non-crossing routing. Anchorage positions on each side of the pivot are what produce the equalizing moment balance, so this is substantive topology, not page placement. The disclosure discloses four cables to the bar and slight pivoting, with no anchorage arrangement.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Each path begins at one of four anchor points spaced along the release balance bar 48, two of them left of the balance bar pivot 50 and two of them right of it, and runs outward and away from the release balance bar 48 to end at one of the four blocks. The four paths do not cross one another." Nearest source: "The four locking pawls are connected by four release cables to a release balance bar mounted on the base frame." The description likewise says only "an anchorage on the release balance bar 48".
findings.fix: Replace with: "Each path begins at one of four anchor points on the release balance bar 48 and runs outward to one of the four blocks, shown schematically."

findings.title: Crank socket open-mouth orientation and closed end in FIG. 4 are untraced
findings.detail: The brief states which end of the socket is open and which is closed and the direction the mouth faces. Under the governing rule, statements about which end of a functional slot or port is open or deeper and its end orientation are substantive even where the geometry is called schematic. The disclosure discloses a crank socket only as the thing the interlock acts on.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A crank socket 38 is drawn to the right of the release handle 52 in the lower part of the drawing area as a short open-ended sleeve seen from the side, its open mouth facing downward and its closed end upward, shown schematically." Nearest source: "A mechanical interlock on the crank socket blocks insertion of the hand crank".
findings.fix: Replace with: "A crank socket 38 is drawn beside the release handle 52 as a short sleeve seen from the side, with one open end that receives the hand crank 36, shown schematically."

findings.title: Extending cover and window inspection to the racks, guide towers and base frame is untraced
findings.detail: The disclosure enumerates exactly what the removable cover gives access to, and the window is disclosed only as the aperture through which the flag is visible. The candidate asserts that the racks, guide towers and base frame are inspectable through the cover and that the windows serve as inspection openings between uses.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "the members that carry the standing load, namely the locking pawls 40, the racks 18, the guide towers 14, and the base frame 10, are inspectable through the removable cover 60 and through the windows 56 between uses." Nearest source: "a removable cover gives access to the worm drive, sprockets, chain, pawls, and cable adjusters without removing the equipment deck" and "a locked-state flag that is visible through a window".
findings.fix: Replace with: "the worm drive, the sprockets, the endless synchronizing chain 30, the locking pawls 40, and the cable adjusters 62 are accessible through the removable cover 60 without removing the equipment deck 12."

findings.title: Equal sprocket tooth counts and equal rack pitch are stated as structure without source support
findings.detail: Equal tooth numbers on the two sprockets and equal pitch on all four racks are specific structural parameters. They are entailed by the disclosed equal-distance travel but are never stated in the source, so as recited they are untraced structure rather than a restatement of the disclosed function.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The front sprocket 26 and the rear sprocket 28 have the same number of teeth, so that the front transverse shaft 22 and the rear transverse shaft 24 also rotate through the same angle." and "Because all four pinions 20 rotate together and all four racks 18 have the same pitch, every corner post 16 travels by the same distance for a given input rotation". Nearest source: "A sprocket on the front shaft, a sprocket on the rear shaft, and one endless synchronizing chain couple the shafts so all four pinions rotate together" and "Turning the crank therefore raises or lowers all four corner posts by the same distance".
findings.fix: Replace the first sentence with: "The endless synchronizing chain 30 constrains the front transverse shaft 22 and the rear transverse shaft 24 to rotate through the same angle." In the second, delete "and all four racks 18 have the same pitch", leaving "Because all four pinions 20 rotate together, every corner post 16 travels by the same distance for a given input rotation".

findings.title: "High-reduction mesh" characterization of the worm engagement is untraced
findings.detail: The description characterizes the worm mesh by its reduction ratio class. The disclosure states only that the worm drive resists back-driving; it says nothing about reduction.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The mesh between the worm of the worm input shaft 32 and the worm wheel 34 is a high-reduction mesh that resists back-driving of the synchronizing transmission by the weight on the equipment deck 12". Nearest source: "The worm drive resists back-driving but is not the only load-holding feature."
findings.fix: Replace with: "The mesh between the worm of the worm input shaft 32 and the worm wheel 34 resists back-driving of the synchronizing transmission by the weight on the equipment deck 12".

findings.title: Compression spring seating between guide tower and pawl is untraced, and is the whole of claim 14
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 14; draft/08-detailed-description.md, first paragraph of "Independent load locks at each guided post"
findings.detail: A specific seating relationship is claimed and described. The disclosure discloses a compression spring that biases the pawl toward the locked position, without any reaction member or seating arrangement.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 14): "wherein the spring biasing each locking pawl is a compression spring seated between the guide tower carrying that locking pawl and that locking pawl." Candidate (description): "A compression spring 44 seated between the guide tower 14 and the locking pawl 40 biases the locking pawl 40 toward the locked position". Nearest source: "A compression spring biases each locking pawl toward the locked position."
findings.fix: Amend claim 14 to read: "The platform of claim 1, wherein the spring biasing each locking pawl is a compression spring." In the description, replace with: "A compression spring 44 biases the locking pawl 40 toward the locked position".

findings.title: Numeral 50 (balance bar pivot) is given two different meanings, and FIG. 4 omits the base-frame mounting the claims require
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, first and third paragraphs of "Equalizing release linkage" and "Method of use"; figures/fig-04.md; draft/09-claims.md claims 1 and 17
findings.detail: In the description, 50 is the pivot by which the balance bar is mounted on the base frame; in FIG. 4 it is the joint at which the bar and the handle turn relative to one another, with no connection to the base frame anywhere on the sheet. A numbered part must mean one thing, and the base-frame mounting is a claimed limitation that the figure fails to depict.
findings.evidence: Description: "a release balance bar 48 is mounted on the base frame 10 on a balance bar pivot 50". FIG. 4: "A balance bar pivot 50 is a small circle with a centre mark at the middle of the release balance bar 48, drawn where the release balance bar 48 crosses the upper end of the release handle 52, so that the bar and the handle turn on the same circle relative to one another." Claim 1: "a release balance bar mounted on the base frame". Source: "a release balance bar mounted on the base frame. A release handle pivots the balance bar... The balance bar can pivot slightly relative to the release handle".
findings.fix: In fig-04.md, replace the balance bar pivot sentence with: "A balance bar pivot 50 is a small circle with a centre mark at the middle of the release balance bar 48, drawn on a short unnumbered support representing the base frame 10, the upper end of the release handle 52 meeting the release balance bar 48 at that circle so that the bar can turn slightly relative to the handle." Also add "the release balance bar 48 being mounted on the base frame 10 at that circle" to the Structures section so the claimed mounting appears on the sheet.

findings.title: Claims 1 and 19 recite "a plurality of" guide towers, reading on two, below the disclosed floor of three
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claims 1 and 19; draft/06-summary.md, first aspect paragraph
findings.detail: The disclosure supports four guided posts and, as a variant, "three or more than four". A two-tower, two-post platform is nowhere disclosed and the disclosed anti-racking and parallel-travel results are not described for it. Claim 16 correctly uses "at least three"; claims 1 and 19 and the summary do not.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 1): "a plurality of upright guide towers carried by the base frame". Candidate (claim 19): "a base frame carrying a plurality of upright guide towers". Nearest source: "the platform uses three or more than four guide towers with one rack, pinion, spring-biased pawl, release cable, and locked-state flag at each guided post" - no passage contemplates two.
findings.fix: In claims 1 and 19 change "a plurality of upright guide towers" to "at least three upright guide towers" and change the dependent recitations "a plurality of posts" to "a post carried by the equipment deck and sliding vertically in each guide tower" (matching claim 16). In draft/06-summary.md change "a plurality of upright guide towers" to "at least three upright guide towers" and "a like plurality of posts" to "a post for each guide tower".

findings.title: FIG. 2 asserts pinion teeth touching four unnumbered blocks and shows no rack 18
findings.detail: The brief introduces four unidentified square blocks and asserts a contact relationship between each pinion's teeth and the nearer side of the adjacent block. The claimed and disclosed relationship is that each pinion meshes with the rack of the post; rack 18 appears nowhere on this sheet, so the sheet asserts a contact with an element of undeclared identity.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A small unnumbered square block sits at each of its four inner corners." and "Each is centred on the shaft it belongs to and its teeth touch the nearer side of the adjacent square block." Source: "A pinion in each guide tower meshes with the rack of that corner post".
findings.fix: Replace with: "A corner post 16 is drawn as a small square block at each of the four inner corners of the boundary outline, each carrying a rack 18 on the side facing the interior of the outline." and "Each pinion 20 is centred on the shaft it belongs to and meshes with the rack 18 of the adjacent corner post 16." Add 16 and 18 to the "Numerals on this sheet" list and add placement entries for them.

findings.title: Cable-length drivers (routing, wear, adjuster seating, temperature) are untraced operating conditions
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, second paragraph of "Equalizing release linkage"
findings.detail: The description recites specific causes of effective-length variation as operating conditions of the invention. The disclosure refers only to "cable-length differences" without cause.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The four release cables 46 are flexible members of finite manufacturing tolerance whose effective lengths change with routing, wear, seating of the cable adjusters 62, and temperature." Nearest source: "The balance bar can pivot slightly relative to the release handle so cable-length differences do not leave one pawl engaged while the other pawls are released."
findings.fix: Replace with: "The four release cables 46 are flexible members whose effective lengths can differ from one another."

findings.title: FIG. 1 verbalizes proportions and shapes beyond a generic outline
findings.detail: FIG. 1 is described in draft/07 as a perspective view, and several of these members are not marked "shown schematically". The brief nonetheless fixes the frame's plan aspect ratio, an identical deck plan outline, and a square post cross section, none of which is disclosed.
findings.evidence: Candidate: base frame "longer from left to right than from front to back"; deck "a flat rectangular slab of the same plan outline as the base frame 10"; "Each corner post 16 is a straight square-section column". Nearest source: "keeping the equipment deck parallel to a rectangular base frame" and "four corner posts that slide vertically in the respective guide towers" - no proportions or post cross section are disclosed.
findings.fix: Delete "longer from left to right than from front to back"; change the deck to "a flat rectangular slab held above the upper ends of the guide towers 14 and parallel to the base frame 10, shown schematically"; change the post to "a straight upright column, shown schematically".

findings.title: FIG. 2 verbalizes relative wheel sizes and axial positions on the shafts
findings.detail: The brief fixes the sprockets and worm wheel as larger than a pinion and places them at stated axial positions left and right of the shaft midpoint. Neither the relative diameters nor the axial positions are disclosed; as written they read as design parameters rather than a placement convention.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A front sprocket 26 is a toothed circle larger than a pinion 20, centred on the front transverse shaft 22 to the left of the middle of that shaft." "A worm wheel 34 is a toothed circle larger than a pinion 20, centred on the front transverse shaft 22 to the right of the middle of that shaft." Nearest source: "A sprocket on the front shaft, a sprocket on the rear shaft, and one endless synchronizing chain couple the shafts"; "The worm input shaft drives a worm wheel fixed to the front transverse shaft."
findings.fix: Delete "larger than a pinion 20" in both sentences and replace the axial qualifiers with "centred on the front transverse shaft 22 between its ends, shown schematically", keeping only the requirement that the rear sprocket 28 lie in the plane of the chain loop with the front sprocket 26.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief describes the pinions as part of a drive "housed in the base frame" while the description mounts each pinion in a guide tower
findings.where: draft/07-drawings.md, FIG. 2 sentence; figures/fig-02.md "View" and boundary outline; draft/08-detailed-description.md third paragraph of "Overall arrangement" and claim 1
findings.detail: The same parts are located differently in two places: the drawing description places the four pinions in the drive housed in the base frame, while the description and claim 1 require a pinion mounted in each guide tower.
findings.evidence: draft/07: "FIG. 2 is a schematic plan view of the synchronized drive housed in the base frame, showing the four pinions..." Description: "A pinion 20 is mounted in each guide tower 14". Claim 1: "a pinion mounted in each guide tower".
findings.fix: Change the FIG. 2 sentence in draft/07-drawings.md to: "FIG. 2 is a schematic plan view of the synchronized drive of the platform, showing the four pinions at the four guide towers, the front and rear transverse shafts, the sprockets, the endless synchronizing chain, the worm input shaft, and the worm wheel." In fig-02.md, describe the boundary outline as representing the base frame 10 with the four guide towers 14 at its inner corners.

findings.title: FIG. 3 is a sectional view with no section line indicated on any source view
findings.detail: FIG. 3 is presented as a vertical sectional view cut on a stated plane, but no section line and no repeated designation appear in FIG. 1 (or FIG. 2) to show where the section is taken, and the drawing description names none. Nothing is inconsistent between the three places because no designation exists at all; the omission is a drawing formality.
findings.evidence: draft/07: "FIG. 3 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view of one guide tower and the corner post sliding in it". fig-03.md: "cut on a vertical plane through the locking pawl of that guide tower". fig-01.md "Structures and relationships" contains no section line and its numeral list is "10, 12, 14, 16, 36, 52, 60, 64".
findings.fix: Either add a designated section line to fig-01.md ("A section line 3-3 is drawn across the front left guide tower 14 in a vertical plane, with arrows and the designation 3-3 at both ends") and change the draft/07 sentence to "FIG. 3 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 1...", or keep FIG. 3 undesignated and change draft/07 to "FIG. 3 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view of one guide tower and the corner post sliding in it, taken on a vertical plane through the locking pawl of that guide tower". Use one option consistently in draft/07 and fig-03.md.

findings.title: FIG. 1 shows the hand crank installed without the pulled release handle the interlock requires
findings.where: figures/fig-01.md, "Structures and relationships"; draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Crank and release interlock"
findings.detail: The brief depicts the hand crank inserted in the base frame while leaving the release handle's state unspecified. Per the disclosed interlock, the crank can only be in place when the handle is in its pulled position, so the sheet should say which state is shown to avoid depicting an impossible condition.
findings.evidence: fig-01: "A hand crank 36 is drawn right of the removable cover 60 as a short horizontal shaft entering the front wall of the base frame 10..." Source: "A mechanical interlock on the crank socket blocks insertion of the hand crank unless the release handle is in its pulled position".
findings.fix: Add to the fig-01.md hand crank paragraph: "The hand crank 36 is shown in place, the release handle 52 being shown in its pulled position as the mechanical interlock 58 requires."

findings.title: Claim 13 lists the release cables among what the removable cover closes
findings.detail: The disclosure enumerates what the cover gives access to; release cables are not in that list, although cable adjusters (which lie in the cables) are. The claim as written recites a cover position over the cables themselves.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "a removable cover closing the base frame over the synchronizing transmission, the locking pawls, and the release cables, removal of the removable cover giving access to the synchronizing transmission, the locking pawls, and the release cables without removal of the equipment deck." Nearest source: "a removable cover gives access to the worm drive, sprockets, chain, pawls, and cable adjusters without removing the equipment deck."
findings.fix: Amend claim 13 to: "The platform of claim 1, further comprising a removable cover closing the base frame over the synchronizing transmission, the locking pawls, and the cable adjusters of the release cables, removal of the removable cover giving access to the synchronizing transmission, the locking pawls, and the cable adjusters without removal of the equipment deck." (Claim 12 already introduces the cable adjuster; make claim 13 depend on claim 12.)
